bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- H2 FY26 Debt to Equity of 0.05 (down from 0.38 in FY22), and Debt Service Coverage Ratio improved to 3.57x in FY26 from 1.09x in FY23, indicating a largely deleveraged balance sheet.
- Net worth grew from ₹1,358 Lakh (FY22) to ₹12,300 Lakh (FY26); H2 FY26 ROE of 12.7% and ROCE of 16.9% (annualised).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Over 21 years of operational experience in MICE and travel, with long-standing relationships with customers and industry stakeholders
- Client roster of over 30 elite brands across BFSI, insurance, automotive, cement and healthcare
- Demonstrated multi-continent execution: FY26 international operations spanned Australasia, South America, Central America and Africa

bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Geopolitical escalation in West Asia — further airspace closures and an oil price surge — Graded Medium probability / High impact. Directly inflates international MICE cost and forces itinerary rerouting; the Company's stated mitigation is an intensified Asia-Pacific and South America footprint with domestic government projects acting as a revenue buffer.
- India-Pakistan border tensions affecting Northern India MICE — Graded Low-Medium probability / Medium impact. Northern India group movements are exposed to renewed border tension; mitigated by geographic diversification to Southern India, Rajasthan and Goa and by advance rebooking policies.
- Currency — INR depreciation against USD/EUR raising international MICE costs — Graded Medium / Medium. A weaker Rupee elevates the cost base of outbound programmes priced in hard currency; mitigated through dynamic pricing models, client cost-sharing agreements and domestic revenue hedging.
- Cost inflation — jet fuel prices and hotel ADR squeezing corporate event budgets — Graded Medium / Medium. Input inflation compresses the client's willingness to spend and the Company's own margin; mitigated by in-house GDS ticketing to lock fares, bulk hotel contracting and dynamic repricing clauses.
- Cybersecurity breaches and data privacy exposure from the Mach Travel platform — Graded Medium probability / High impact, and structurally new as the Company moves from B2B event management into a consumer-facing digital platform holding traveller data. Mitigation is an internal auditor appointment, a cybersecurity framework per the DPDP Act 2023, and SSL/encryption.
- Revenue concentration in select clients or government mandates — Graded Medium probability / High impact — the clearest structural risk, given single mandates of the scale of the Punjab Tirth Yatra programme. Mitigation cited is a 30+ brand client base and a Government Projects Division that diversifies the revenue mix.
- Execution risk on large-scale government programmes — Graded Low-Medium probability / High impact, named against the Punjab Tirth Yatra programme. Mitigation relies on an experienced operations team, a sub-contractor network and a multi-vendor logistics model. The same mandates also lengthen the working-capital cycle through advances and billing cycles.
- Regulatory change — MICE-related GST structure or aviation policy — Graded Low probability / Medium impact. Mitigated by active engagement with IATA, IATO and ADTOI and by diversified revenue streams.
- No Risk Management Committee is constituted at Board level — The Board states there is no legal requirement to constitute a Risk Management Committee and instead relies on risk considerations being embedded in strategic and operational decision-making under a Risk Management Policy — a governance structure worth noting given the scale-up in government mandates and the move into consumer data.

business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Incorporated in 2004 as a MICE company, evolved into an integrated travel and mobility platform serving enterprise, institutional, government and retail travel requirements.
- PAN India presence with 400+ employees, 20+ years of experience and event management across 25+ countries; affiliated with IATA, IATO, PATA and ADTOI.
- Cites strong, established industry relationships with airlines and hotels as a strategic advantage enabling smoother deals and better negotiation terms, plus a long-standing corporate customer base supporting B2C cross-sell via brand recognition.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Rebranding] Company renamed from Mach Conferences and Events Limited to Mach Travel Solutions Limited in 2026, reflecting the pivot from MICE to an integrated travel platform.
- [Disruption] FY26 EBITDA and PAT margins improved despite temporary disruptions from Operation Sindoor and Middle East geopolitical developments, per the Chairman & Managing Director's letter.
- [Investor Relations] Adfactors Investor Relations (Vaibhav Gupta, Yash Sanghavi) acts as IR advisor alongside Company Secretary & Compliance Officer Yashashvi Srivastava.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Mach designs and delivers end-to-end Meetings, Incentives, Conferences and Exhibitions (MICE) programmes, corporate travel management, government and institutional assignments, and B2C spiritual and leisure travel. Corporate clients span BFSI, insurance, automotive, cement, pharma and healthcare, while the government vertical executes large-scale pilgrimage management and official hospitality for state and central events. In FY26 the Company organised events for over 30 elite brands and ran international programmes across four continents, while building an in-house GDS/IATA ticketing capability and a retail travel portal.

- **Corporate Travel Desk:** Corporate Self Booking Tool
- **Government Projects:** Large-scale pilgrimage management, Official hospitality for state/central events
- **B2C Spiritual & Leisure:** Helicopter Char Dham and Do Dham packages, Cordelia Cruise distribution, 'Mach Travel' OTA portal

outlook.body: Targeting record revenues in FY27, with a focus on expanding B2C segment, widening footprint across India, and strengthening corporate, government, and institutional relationships.
outlook.title: Guidance / outlook

outlook.body: ₹142+ Cr order pipeline, with multiple large domestic and international mandates
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Expansion into new markets, growing demand for travel and tourism, and increasing adoption of digital technologies
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Transform from a predominantly MICE-focused organisation into a diversified, integrated travel solutions platform spanning the travel value chain — the stated rationale for the change of name from 'Mach Conferences and Events Limited' to 'Mach Travel Solutions Limited'.
- Expand presence in government and institutional programmes, building a scalable government projects portfolio on the back of compliance and logistical discipline.
- Strengthen leadership in corporate MICE services, retaining end-to-end travel logistics, event production and on-ground execution across global destinations as the key differentiator.
- Gradually build a broader travel services ecosystem across corporate travel, B2B travel services, B2C travel platforms, leisure travel, inbound tourism and destination management.
- Invest in organisational capability — leadership depth, management bandwidth, process streamlining, operational scalability and technology-driven solutions to improve service delivery and customer experience.
- Pivot geographic mix after the FY26 northern-India disruption: defer Northern India group movements and accelerate into Southern and Western India corridors and domestic government mandates.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Mach's expansion in FY26 is platform and footprint build-out rather than physical capacity. The digital transformation strategy is anchored by the planned launch of 'Mach Travel', a comprehensive OTA portal offering flights, hotels, cruise bookings, spiritual tour packages and visa services, described as 90% ready and in a testing phase pending launch; it is designed to convert a captive audience of over 100,000 annual travellers into lifetime retail customers. Alongside it, in-house GDS/IATA ticketing is fully enabled to eliminate intermediary margins, a Corporate Travel Desk offering one-click managed travel and policy automation for MNC, GCC and MSME clients is operational, an AI-powered delegate management capability covering predictive pricing, automated delegate communications and AI-assisted itinerary planning is in development, and a cybersecurity framework aligned to the DPDP Act 2023 is being put in place with an internal auditor appointed. On the service footprint, the Company has exclusive helicopter-based Char Dham and Do Dham packages targeting HNIs and senior citizens, and is a key distributor for Cordelia Cruises, positioning it for India's cruise tourism market. The Company describes itself as an asset-light MICE, travel and event management services business that does not carry physical inventory, and no plant, capacity or rupee capital-expenditure quantum is disclosed in this bundle.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Rising corporate travel demand, increasing globalisation of Indian businesses and continued investment in tourism infrastructure are expected to support long-term industry growth.
- Consumer preference for experiential spending has proven resilient despite geopolitical volatility; the global MICE industry was valued at USD 937.43 billion in 2025 and is projected to reach USD 2,030.95 billion by 2034 at a 9.0% CAGR.
- India remains the fastest-growing major economy, with GDP growth projected at 6.5-7.0% for FY26 by the Reserve Bank of India and FY27 real GDP growth of 6.8-7.2% by most multilateral agencies.
- Government infrastructure emphasis — targeting 350 operational airports by 2047, a highway network beyond 2 lakh km and development of convention infrastructure — provides a structurally supportive environment for the organised travel and MICE industry.
- H2 FY26 recovery was anchored by the Punjab Tirth Yatra mandate, the New Zealand MICE contract, IFFI 2025 hospitality and the pipeline recovery of deferred BFSI and insurance incentive programmes across Bali, Kenya, Argentina and Mexico.
- Cost headwinds on international MICE: jet fuel prices up an estimated 85-100% versus pre-conflict levels, Middle East airspace closures forcing itinerary rerouting, Europe-Asia flight times extended by 40-90 minutes, and the Rupee breaching INR 95/USD.
- Demand redirection effects — Indian arrivals to Azerbaijan fell 70% and to Turkey 38% year-on-year, redirecting demand to Southeast Asia, the Gulf and European alternatives, and a demand pivot to Asia-Pacific after Middle East disruption.
- Management states that a diversified project pipeline and disciplined execution, together with operational efficiency, strong vendor partnerships and prudent cost management, allowed stable revenues and healthy margins through the disruption.
- Mandate from the Government of Punjab to manage the Chief Minister's Tirth Yatra initiative, involving the movement and management of approximately 1,85,000 pilgrims over multiple phases.
- Several government assignments of varying scale secured in a relatively short span, described as demonstrating ability to execute high-impact programmes with strong compliance and logistical discipline.
- Multiple high-value domestic and international travel programmes secured during the year, including large corporate incentive movements and conferences involving hundreds of participants.
- H2 FY26 book anchored by the Punjab Tirth Yatra mandate, the New Zealand MICE contract and IFFI 2025 hospitality, plus deferred BFSI and insurance incentive programmes across Bali, Kenya, Argentina and Mexico returning to the pipeline.
